questions: Is there any constraint on the number of stones moved from bag A to bag B in a single operation? Can we move any positive integer number up to the current stones in bag A, or must we move all stones?
Can we choose the same bag as both A and B in an operation?

Are the bags considered distinguishable for the purpose of the XOR? That is, does swapping contents between bags produce a different sequence (B_1,...,B_N) even if the multiset of stone counts is the same?
Is the operation allowed to result in a bag having zero stones? And can we later move stones from a bag that currently has zero stones?

Does the XOR operation consider the sequence (B_1,...,B_N) after operations, or just the multiset of values? The problem states 'B_1 ⊕ B_2 ⊕ ... ⊕ B_N', which is order-independent, but the labeling might affect which values are assigned to which index.
Are there any constraints on the total number of operations? The prompt says 'any number of times, possibly zero', but is there an implicit bound like not exceeding total stones?
Can we move stones from bag B to bag A in the same operation, or is the operation strictly one-directional (from A to B only)?
Is the goal to count distinct possible XOR values over all possible sequences of operations, considering all possible choices at each step, or only those reachable via some sequence?
